subject: Urgent: Evergreen Health — latency, errors, and throughput regressions after model upgrade
messages:
From: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@evergreenhealth.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: ops@evergreenhealth.com
Date: 2026-08-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Urgent: latency & errors after model upgrade

Hi Laura,

We pushed the v2.1 model with the new quant profile (q-v2-low) at 08:45 PT as part of the scheduled upgrade. Within ~20 minutes we started seeing a sharp rise in P95 latency (from ~210ms to 780ms), error rate (5% 5xx), and a drop in sustained throughput on the inference route for clinical triage. This is impacting live traffic — roughly ~12% of requests are failing with 5xx and many more are timing out and falling back.

I attached our perf extract (perf_run_20260829_log.txt) and included a few sample request IDs. Notes:
- Spike correlates exactly with the model rollout window.
- Errors look like decode stalls / worker timeouts in the Redwood runtime (we saw process restarts).
- We are on Redwood Dedicated; committed throughput is critical for our SLAs.

This is customer-impacting — please escalate immediately. We need one of your engineers on an incident bridge and a clear mitigation plan (rollback? throttle?). Our execs are asking for an update in 90 minutes.

CC'ing procurement for visibility on credit/SLAs.

Thanks,
Carlos
Director of Engineering, Evergreen Health
ops@evergreenhealth.com

Attachment: perf_run_20260829_log.txt (6.2KB)

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: latency & errors after model upgrade — initial triage

Quick triage notes from the bridge logs and customer perf file:
- Confirmed: q-v2-low quant profile + v2.1 model were rolled together. No other runtime config changes were deployed.
- Symptom: increased tokenization length in a subset of requests (EOS handling edge-case) triggers additional KV cache misses and forces a long decode path; combined with a small regression in the new attention kernel this yields head-of-line stalls and worker timeouts.
- Runtime reaction: some workers are crashing and restarting under the heavier decode CPU fallback, which explains the transient 5xx spike and throughput collapse.

Suggested immediate mitigation (ordered):
1) Rollback quant profile to q-v1.9 (this is a profile-only change; safe to apply and immediate to revert). I have a diff that reverts the policy tested (quant-profile-v2.diff).
2) Temporarily increase Dedicated burst capacity + CPU headroom for the inference pool for 60 minutes to buy time for a graceful rollout.
3) Post-rollback: run a smoke test across the clinical-triage route and release a staged canary to 10% before full re-cut.

I can apply the rollback now if we have permission. If not, we will degrade SLOs for a longer remediation window.

Attachment: quant-profile-v2.diff (2.4KB)

—Rishi
Lead, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Subject: Action plan and mitigation update — rolling back quant profile at 13:30 PT

Carlos / Evergreen team —

Thanks for your patience on the bridge. Summary and next steps:

Root cause (short): q-v2-low quant profile + v2.1 model introduced a decode path regression for a subset of inputs (EOS/tokenization edge-case) that increased decode time and triggered worker restarts.

Actions taken at 13:30 PT (complete):
- Rolled back quant profile from q-v2-low to q-v1.9 across your inference pool.
- Increased Dedicated burst capacity by 30% for the next 60 minutes to stabilize requests while we validate.
- Rishi and team ran a smoke test against 2000 live-like requests; P95 fell back to ~230ms and 5xxs dropped below 0.5% in the test window.

Next steps (the next 48 hours):
- We will run an extended validation sweep against production traffic during low hours and prepare a validated q-v2a with the decode fix.
- Proposed exec sync (30 minutes) at 16:00 PT to review compensation/credit and a postmortem schedule.
- We'll provide a formal RCA and preventative actions within 3 business days.

Offer: we recognize this impacted SLA. We will propose a one-time credit for the impacted window and include it in the postmortem package. Procurement (cc'd) — Laura and I will coordinate the credit proposal and DocuSign.

Let me know if you want the rollback undone (we do not recommend that currently). We'll keep the capacity bump for 60 minutes and monitor.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
Phone: +1-415-555-0183

Laura — thanks for the quick response and the rollback. Metrics look much better from our monitoring (we still see a small tail but within tolerances).

Please confirm two items before we close the incident:
1) The exact SLO window affected and the time range you will propose for the credit (procurement needs precise timestamps).
2) We expect a 3-day postmortem with root cause, remediation, and a test checklist for future quant/profile rollouts. Please include a small runbook so our SREs can understand the fallback criteria.

We'll be on the exec sync at 16:00 PT. Appreciate the rapid coordination.

—Carlos
Director of Engineering, Evergreen Health
